issues.legal_issue: An able-bodied husband remains obliged to maintain a wife who is unable to maintain herself merely because he claims to have no current income.
material_facts: The courts below concurrently found that the wife was unemployed and unable to maintain herself.
The husband was educated and able-bodied, and had previously worked in Canada.
The husband claimed that he had resigned from his employment and had no source of income, but did not produce evidence establishing his unemployment or inability to earn.
issues.conclusion: The husband’s bare claim that he had no source of income did not absolve him of his obligation to maintain his wife; the High Court’s finding of liability was unexceptionable.
issues.legal_principle: Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure provides a means of support for a wife unable to maintain herself. An able-bodied person is presumed capable of earning enough to discharge the obligation of maintaining his wife, and must show cogent grounds for inability to earn for reasons beyond his control. The Court relied on Chander Prakash v. Shrimati Shila Rani, AIR 1968 Del 174, and Bhuwan Mohan Singh v. Meena, AIR 2014 SC 2875, including the principle that maintenance enables a wife to live with dignity and that an able-bodied husband cannot evade his duty by a bare assertion of having no income.

rule.if: maintenance_claim and wife_unable_to_maintain_herself and husband_able_bodied and husband_unemployment_claim_unsubstantiated

predicates.maintenance_claim: A proceeding seeking maintenance for a wife was brought.
predicates.wife_unable_to_maintain_herself: The wife was found unable to support herself.
predicates.husband_able_bodied: The husband was found physically capable of working and earning.
predicates.husband_unemployment_claim_unsubstantiat: The husband claimed to be unemployed or without income but did not establish that claim with evidence.

issues.definition: When a maintenance claim concerns a wife unable to support herself and an able-bodied husband whose claim of unemployment is unsubstantiated, the husband remains obliged to maintain her.

issues.legal_issue: The amount of maintenance must be determined by considering the payer’s circumstances and conduct rather than relying solely on a notional minimum-income estimate.
material_facts: The appeal challenged the amount of maintenance awarded in a maintenance proceeding.
The husband was highly qualified and able-bodied, had previously earned a substantial salary while working abroad, and had taken an unsubstantiated position that he was unemployed from 2010.
The husband had protracted the maintenance proceedings, which had continued for many years.
The Supreme Court had earlier directed interim maintenance of Rs.20,000 per month, and the Court considered the payer’s family living standard, inflation, and the high cost of living.
The High Court had calculated the husband’s presumed income using current minimum wages and awarded Rs.9,000 per month from December 2010.
issues.conclusion: The Court held that using notional minimum wages as the basis for the maintenance amount was untenable. It increased maintenance to Rs.20,000 per month from January 2010 and Rs.25,000 per month from 1 June 2018 until further orders, with amounts already paid or deposited to be adjusted; the enhanced amount was payable within eight weeks.
issues.legal_principle: In fixing maintenance under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the court must consider the payer’s living standard and family circumstances, past conduct in delaying proceedings, the credibility of a claim of unemployment, previous income, and current inflation and cost of living. The Court rejected a calculation based on notional minimum wages alone and took account of its earlier interim-maintenance order in the same litigation. The general purpose of maintenance as support enabling a wife to live with dignity was also consistent with Bhuwan Mohan Singh v. Meena, AIR 2014 SC 2875.

rule.if: appeal_concerning_maintenance_quantum and payer_highly_qualified_and_able_bodied and prior_income_substantial and unemployment_claim_unsubstantiated and proceedings_protracted and living_costs_increased

predicates.appeal_concerning_maintenance_quantum: An appeal challenged the amount awarded in a maintenance proceeding.
predicates.payer_highly_qualified_and_able_bodied: The person required to pay maintenance was found highly qualified and physically capable of earning.
predicates.prior_income_substantial: The payer had previously earned a substantial income.
predicates.unemployment_claim_unsubstantiated: The payer claimed to be unemployed or without income but did not establish that claim with evidence.
predicates.proceedings_protracted: The payer’s conduct contributed to a prolonged maintenance proceeding.
predicates.living_costs_increased: The court took account of increased inflation or the high cost of living.

issues.definition: In an appeal over maintenance quantum, when the payer is qualified and able-bodied, had substantial prior income, has not substantiated unemployment, proceedings were prolonged, and living costs have increased, the amount is increased after considering the relevant circumstances.
